where: Sunken Solarium Lumenary (Lucan Pyre's flooded stage hall) + the Last-Warm-Day festival bed
mood: Drowned Halls: the same sun-garden with the water winning - cooler, lonelier, a summer theme recoloured into its relative minor; bittersweet warmth spent knowing it fades.
core_styles: E minor relative to G major
spacious pulse-wave lead with long notes and rests, sinking phrases that do not always climb back
slow submerged low harp arpeggio rolling like deep water
cool string pad with a warm golden glow underneath
deep synth bass swelling like a slow tide
minimal percussion: soft low thud and occasional droplet-like tick

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {a hushed entrance into a flooded hall: low watery harp ripples, a single droplet tick, a cool pad opening, the lead's first long note hanging in the echo}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the drowned-halls melody in E minor: a rising leap that sinks back down a step short of home, long notes with air between them, slow tide in the bass}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {the melody again, now answered by a soft music-box counter-line and a fuller warm pad, as if the stored daylight glows a little brighter under the water}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: the clouds part into G and C major - a bittersweet golden swell, warm and a little defiant, the lead singing higher like a last warm day, then dimming to minor}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the E minor melody returns, quiet and lonely; the last bar leads straight back into the main theme, no ending}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme

_stall_note: deliberately sparse interior: one ~4 s hush is part of the cue (dead_air.py allows up to max_stall)
